subject: Proof & Probe Playbook: acceptance KPI checkpoints
messages:
From: Alex Norman <alex.norman@bridgepointhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Ops <procurement@bridgepointhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot scope — MAP & acceptance criteria

Kim, Rishi — thanks again for the demo last week. Our stakeholders (clinical ops + infra) want a short, concrete MAP we can take to procurement this week. Two asks from my side: 1) a compact list of acceptance tests we can run during the 30-day pilot (including pass thresholds), and 2) a minimal set of exit gates that would prevent us from moving to contract if not met.

We sketched internal priorities: latency under 350ms p95 for triage flows, 95% intent accuracy on our 120-case test set, and no PII leakage in the sampling (we'll provide redacted examples). Can you confirm what you need from us to lock the MAP, and suggest a target calendar for tests + signoff?

I'll attach our trial checklist and a spreadsheet of 120 sample prompts. If we can get this finalized by Friday it keeps procurement on track for the month-end approval.

—Alex
BridgePoint Health

Attachments: BP_trial_prompts.xlsx (stated), BridgePoint-trial-checklist.pdf (stated)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Norman <alex.norman@bridgepointhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot scope — MAP & acceptance criteria

Alex — thanks, this is helpful. Drafting a concise MAP now. Quick answers up front: we can run a 30-day pilot with a focused acceptance run (10-day smoke + 14-day regression window + 6-day stakeholder review). For your stated priorities I propose the following acceptance tests (summary):

- Latency: p95 end-to-end < 350ms measured over a moving 1h window during production-like load. Fail if p95 > 450ms for two consecutive measurement windows.
- Accuracy: intent classification concordance >= 95% over your 120-case test set (we'll use blinded grading). Fail if concordance < 90% after two remediation attempts.
- Safety / PII: zero confirmed PII exfiltration incidents in a 14-day sample (we run automated redaction checks + manual spot audits). Any confirmed leakage is an immediate hard stop until remediated.
- Throughput: sustained rate of X RPS (we'll confirm exact number with your infra team) during a 2-hour load window without queued requests > 5s.

Exit gates (minimum):
1) Critical safety breach (PII leak) — require remediation and security review.
2) Accuracy below 90% after remediation attempts.
3) Latency consistently above 450ms p95 and not remediable within the pilot runbook.

I attached a working MAP spreadsheet (BP_MAP_v2.xlsx) and an "acceptance-test-vectors.pdf" that describes the test harness. Ask: can you confirm the RPS target and the SRE contact for the load window? Also, who will do the blinded grading of the 120-case set (you or a cross-functional reviewer)?

I'll put Marissa on the thread to coordinate calendar / evidence collection. If we agree, we'll lock the MAP and share a DocuSign-ready mutual-action summary for signatures.

—Kim
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: BP_MAP_v2.xlsx (working MAP), acceptance-test-vectors.pdf (test harness spec)
From: Alex Norman <alex.norman@bridgepointhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Procurement Ops <procurement@bridgepointhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot scope — MAP & acceptance criteria

Kim — this looks good and clear. Procurement confirms they need the acceptance checklist embedded in the MAP doc (single page) plus a signoff schedule. Answers:

- RPS target: 12 RPS sustained for the 2-hour window (peak testing). SRE contact: satish.patel@bridgepointhealth.com (cc'd).
- Blinded grading: we'll have a clinical reviewer (Dr. Elena Ruiz) and a product SME jointly grade the 120 cases; we'll share the anonymized rubric by Thursday.

Two small asks from procurement: can you add an explicit acceptance timeline (dates) and a contingency clause that defines rollout hold for issues discovered during the 14-day regression window? They want explicit remediation windows and an escrow-style fallback (manual routing to legacy triage if a critical gating failure occurs).

If you can update BP_MAP_v2 with the dates and contingency language, procurement can take the packet to their legal review on Monday. We're aiming to sign the MAP as part of the MSA addendum next Friday.

—Alex

On Wed, Jul 8, 2026 at 11:02 AM Satish Patel <satish.patel@bridgepointhealth.com> wrote:
> Satish here — I can coordinate infra for the load window and will provision a staging VPC. Please loop me in on exact test times.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Norman <alex.norman@bridgepointhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Procurement Ops <procurement@bridgepointhealth.com>, Satish Patel <satish.patel@bridgepointhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2026 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot scope — MAP & acceptance criteria

Alex / team — thanks for the clear answers. I've updated the MAP spreadsheet with explicit dates and contingency language (see notes tab). High-level plan locked below (dates are provisional until we confirm staging windows with Satish):

- Week A (2026-07-12 to 2026-07-21): 10-day smoke (connectivity + golden-path tests). Evidence: automated logs, p95 latency dashboard, sample transcripts (redacted).
- Week B (2026-07-22 to 2026-08-04): 14-day regression validation across the 120-case set (blinded grading by BridgePoint reviewers). Evidence: grading spreadsheet + discrepancy register.
- Week C (2026-08-05 to 2026-08-10): Stakeholder review and signoff period (clinical + operations + procurement). Expectation: documented signoff in HubSpot + DocuSign MAP attachment.

Contingency clause (short): if any critical gating failure occurs during Week B, Redwood will pause the rollout and open a remediation sprint. Remediation window: 5 business days for a code/config fix; if not resolvable, BridgePoint may elect fallback to manual routing for impacted flows. Detailed language is in the MAP "contingency" cell.

Next steps for us (Redwood):
- Rishi will produce a short runbook describing measurement methodology for latency and throughput.
- I'll export the one-page acceptance checklist and push a DocuSign packet to Alex for signature.

Alex — can you confirm the staging times for the load window (Satish), and confirm who the single DocuSign signee will be on your side? Once we have that, we'll send the MAP packet to legal.

Thanks — Marissa
Principal Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood-eval-questions.docx (evidence checklist), updated_BP_MAP_v2.xlsx (with dates + contingency notes)
